title: Superficial muscles of the anterior forearm (anterior)
lab: Forearm, Cubital Fossa, and Elbow Joint
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Humeral head: medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor origin). Ulnar head: coronoid process of the ulna.
Middle of the lateral surface of the radius.
Pronates the forearm and helps flex the elbow.
hy: The median nerve enters the forearm between its two heads and can be compressed there (pronator syndrome).

rows: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor origin).
Flexes and abducts the hand at the wrist.
Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor origin).
Weakly flexes the wrist and tightens the palmar aponeurosis.

structures.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris muscle
objects: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r
Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r

rows: Humeral head: medial epicondyle of the humerus. Ulnar head: olecranon and posterior border of the ulna.
Pisiform and, through ligaments, the hook of the hamate and the base of the 5th metacarpal.
Flexes and adducts the hand at the wrist.
hy: The ulnar nerve enters the forearm between its two heads, behind the medial epicondyle (cubital tunnel), a common site of compression.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis muscle
objects: Humero-ulnar head of flexor digitorum superficialis.r
Radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis.r

rows: Humero-ulnar head: medial epicondyle of the humerus and coronoid process of the ulna. Radial head: upper half of the anterior border of the radius.
Sides of the middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5.
Flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of digits 2 to 5. Helps flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and the wrist.
Upper two thirds of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
Lateral surface of the distal radius, just above the styloid process.
Flexes the elbow, most strongly when the forearm is midway between pronation and supination.
hy: The brachioradialis reflex tests C5 and C6.
